decisions.id: DECISION: why the screen cannot meet another spelling
decisions.summary: every writer serializes with serde_json compact or copies bytes, and serde_json never escapes a letter
decisions.why: This is a factual premise, labeled as an observation with its method (each writer's code read). It decides nothing beyond the screen. It is the ground for the limitation below and is weighed there.

decisions.id: DECISION: ACCEPTED LIMITATION, an ev spelled with a \u escape
decisions.summary: a line whose ev is written with a JSON \u escape is kept by the full parse but dropped by the screen, so a reversal on it would be missed
decisions.why: This is a case the general behavior ('keeps exactly the rows the full parse keeps') does not cover, so it is ruled as an exception and presumed wrong. The reversal tripwire is feature 375's requirement, and nothing in this request asks for it. Judged against the purpose anyway, the exception removes no protection. The tripwire watches Edits that the hooks log, and the block reads every writer it names as serde_json compact output or a byte-for-byte copy. serde_json escapes only a quote, a backslash or a control character, so 'PreToolUse' (printable ASCII) has one spelling from any writer that escapes no more than JSON requires, not only the three listed. The survey found the literal in all 9,176 of 9,176 kept lines across 485,165 lines of the 34 real logs, and the differential found 0 of 1,937 lists differing. So the excepted case is a line no writer produces. Leaving it is no wrong outcome on any real log, and by constitution XIV's definition of a defect it does not leave a defect. It is one case, so there is no bundling. The writer census is the block's observation, not mine (the bundle excludes the repository), and it says how each writer was read, not what search found the set. The ruling rests on the serializer argument and the survey, not on the list being complete. 'EDIT has carried the same limit since T383' and the go-ahead were not weighed either way.

blocks: ### T458 (found by T443, its Found and left: the reversal index's rebuild, a new, refiled or rotated log's first Edit, was 101.6 / 180.4 ms of `event-log-hooks` against 20.5 / 30.5 warm, measured 2026-11-27 under load1 23 to 25 (`t443-cold.tsv`): the build parsed every line holding `"Edit"`)
### T458 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.id: T458 Approach: the second literal screen
decisions.summary: indexed parses a line only if it also holds the text "PreToolUse" (memmem before UTF-8 decode), on top of T383's "Edit" screen
decisions.why: Performance work on a hook, which the GM asked to come first (2026-11-20, 'can we in general priotitize performance improvements going forward?'; FR-013). It keeps the rows the full parse keeps on every line any writer produces. The differential shows 0 of 1,937 lists differing cold, warm and grown, and it goes red on a wrong screen.

decisions.id: T458 Approach: indexed returns whether it parsed
decisions.summary: a bool return so a test can count the build's parses
decisions.why: Its only use is to let a test prove the screen does what the task claims, so it enforces the task. No behavior changes.

decisions.id: T458 Approach: oracle and differential left unscreened
decisions.summary: the test-only full parse and the differential keep parsing every line
decisions.why: This keeps the proof from being circular. It changes no behavior, and no guard message changes.

decisions.id: DECISION: the literal is the quoted value, not the field
decisions.summary: screen on "PreToolUse", not "ev":"PreToolUse"
decisions.why: A rendering choice. The quoted value alone keeps every line the field spelling keeps, plus any line with whitespace around the colon, so it drops nothing more. It is pinned by a test that goes red on the field-spelling mutant.

decisions.id: DECISION: why the screen cannot meet another spelling
decisions.summary: every writer serializes with serde_json compact or copies bytes, and serde_json never escapes a letter
decisions.why: This is a factual premise, labeled as an observation with its method (each writer's code read). It decides nothing beyond the screen. It is the ground for the limitation below and is weighed there.

decisions.id: DECISION: ACCEPTED LIMITATION, an ev spelled with a \u escape
decisions.summary: a line whose ev is written with a JSON \u escape is kept by the full parse but dropped by the screen, so a reversal on it would be missed
decisions.why: This is a case the general behavior ('keeps exactly the rows the full parse keeps') does not cover, so it is ruled as an exception and presumed wrong. The reversal tripwire is feature 375's requirement, and nothing in this request asks for it. Judged against the purpose anyway, the exception removes no protection. The tripwire watches Edits that the hooks log, and the block reads every writer it names as serde_json compact output or a byte-for-byte copy. serde_json escapes only a quote, a backslash or a control character, so 'PreToolUse' (printable ASCII) has one spelling from any writer that escapes no more than JSON requires, not only the three listed. The survey found the literal in all 9,176 of 9,176 kept lines across 485,165 lines of the 34 real logs, and the differential found 0 of 1,937 lists differing. So the excepted case is a line no writer produces. Leaving it is no wrong outcome on any real log, and by constitution XIV's definition of a defect it does not leave a defect. It is one case, so there is no bundling. The writer census is the block's observation, not mine (the bundle excludes the repository), and it says how each writer was read, not what search found the set. The ruling rests on the serializer argument and the survey, not on the list being complete. 'EDIT has carried the same limit since T383' and the go-ahead were not weighed either way.

decisions.id: T458 Approach: the task line's 101.6 ms not compared
decisions.summary: before and after are measured as interleaved arms at load1 about 7, not against the task line's figure at load1 23 to 25
decisions.why: A measurement choice. Both arms ran under the same load, the comparison is fair, and it is stated openly.

decisions.why: It depends on T443's index, and as performance work it goes ahead of non-performance work (FR-013).

blocks: ### T459 (found by 451 T443's review, 2026-11-27, by reading: a hook killed between the reversal index's temporary write and its rename leaves a `.<feature>.idx.<pid>.<n>.tmp` in `<events dir>/reversal/` that nothing removes; none seen in T443's runs)
### T459 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: The sweep of old temporary index files runs when an index is written (store), never on a read.
decisions.why: A defect fix (a killed hook's .tmp left in <events dir>/reversal/) under the feature's fix-as-we-go and the GM's 2026-11-22 'clean up after ourselves in terms of the file system'. Running it at the one writer is the mechanism, not a narrowing: a leftover of a few hundred KB lives at most until the next write in the directory, which reads no map, contradicts no finding and costs no time (the GM's 2026-11-26 principle: time saved over disk). No defect is left.

decisions.summary: Every feature's temporary file in the directory is swept, by its exact name form (.<stem>.idx.<pid>.<n>.tmp, digits), older than SWEEP_AGE; other names and unreadable ages are left.
decisions.why: Widens the fix to cover a feature whose index is never written again, so it serves the defect's purpose; the exact-form match keeps the sweep from touching anything that is not a leftover of this writer. Nothing the request asks for is excluded.

decisions.summary: SWEEP_AGE is one hour, a knob (GUESS, make tunables).
decisions.why: A tunable bound on a value no research or GM word settles; the GM's 2026-10-25 words allow a knob where nothing indicates a value. It is set far past a live writer's life (about 12 ms, one-shot label 2026-11-27 with its results file), so it keeps T443's invariant that no running writer's file is removed.

blocks: ### T462 (the round arbiter's process-fault on `round:spec-fidelity|plan:451-time-retro-and-efficiency#T448@3`, 2026-11-27T08:00Z: a blank task stub counted plan-review rounds)
### T462 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: A task section is UNWRITTEN when every one of its own blocks is byte for byte a block of the make task-add template (plan::template::stub_block); writing one block makes the whole section written.
decisions.why: Neither the GM's request nor 451's spec says anything about stub sections or about how plan-review rounds are counted. This is the definition the fix depends on, and it errs toward review: one changed block makes the whole section owed. It narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: make plan-delta's keys drop an unwritten section's blocks, after the BLOCKED keys are merged in, so the stub leaves the bundle, its blocks-<tasks> name and the guard's round count.
decisions.why: The defect fixed is a check refusing good work: T448's empty stub held every 451 plan-delta dispatch behind its rounds. Fixing it serves 'Fewer plan re-rounds' (improvement 4) and FR-013's builders' loop. A stub has no plan text to review. Its review is still owed once it is written, because verdicts are keyed by digest.

decisions.summary: The feature-wide judgment (judge_held with no scope) also drops unwritten sections, so plan owed and plan-delta agree. A scoped judgment keeps its own tasks' stubs owed, so ticking a stub's own task still owes its review.
decisions.why: This keeps the two readers consistent and keeps enforcement where it matters: the stub's own tick is still refused. Nothing unreviewed can be ticked. Within.

decisions.summary: The guard's plan round counter (review_round_hooks::plan_rounds) stops at a review row that names the task's stub first heading, as it stops at a CLEAR. A section filled after riding in bundles counts its rounds from zero.
decisions.why: A round in which the section was the template judged none of its text, so counting it against the section's cap counted a round that never happened. That is the arbiter's process-fault and the T451 case the section measured. Removing the miscount narrows nothing the GM asked, and the cap on the section's real rounds is unchanged. Within.

decisions.summary: Accepted limitation: stub-era rows are recognized by the stub's first heading, not by block bytes. So a section whose heading still reads (<why: ...>) while its body is written counts no rounds until the heading changes. A row text digest was priced and not taken.
decisions.why: What goes uncounted: plan-review rounds of a section whose body is written but whose first heading is still the template's. For those rounds the five-round cap does not trip and arbiter escalation is delayed. Nothing passes unreviewed. Verdicts are keyed by the section's digest, so the filled text is still owed its review. The block also states that the approach gate's placeholder check refuses the tick while a <...> placeholder stands. I did not measure that state, and T448's rows show that placeholder text does ride in bundles. The cost is delayed escalation, never bad work passing or good work refused, so it is no defect under XIV v2.36.0. Neither the request nor the spec reaches round-counter granularity. So it is within, not a narrowing of anything asked. This is a second stub test (the heading) beside the one stub_block test that items 2 and 7 name; that is a note, not a finding.

decisions.summary: An arbiter accept or process-fault on a plan round records no verdict for a named task whose section is unwritten (record::split_unwritten). make arbiter-ruled reports no verdict recorded and says the section owes its first review once written.
decisions.why: This carves an exception into 451 T92 / 385 T16, which make an accept or process-fault stand as the named task's verdict. Those are earlier tasks' rules; the GM's request and 451's spec say nothing about them, so this is within what was asked. On substance, a verdict on template text would approve no plan, and D1 explains why an unwritten section needs no count reset. No outcome the GM asked for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: A process-fault on a WRITTEN section still records its verdict, because that CLEAR row is what restarts a written section's round count. Without it the section re-trips the cap at the same round.
decisions.why: The plan declines to widen T462-f to every process-fault, which keeps the existing rule. A filled section still owes its own first review by digest. Within.

decisions.summary: Found and left: T448's stub CLEAR verdicts already in plan-review.json stay as they are.
decisions.why: They change no outcome: the filled text is owed by digest, and an unfilled tick is refused by the approach gate. By XIV's definition a record that changes no outcome is no defect, so leaving it is within.

decisions.summary: T462 is filed as performance work ([perf], 451 FR-013), because a held plan-delta dispatch is builders waiting.
decisions.why: FR-013 counts a task that makes the builders' loop faster as performance work. Unblocking every held plan-delta dispatch is that. Within.
